statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r = true if and only if there exist an integer k and indices i_0, ..., i_{k-1} such that: 2 <= k <= n; i_0, ..., i_{k-1} are pairwise distinct and each lies in [0, n-1]; for every j with 0 <= j < k-1, next(i_j) = i_{j+1}, and next(i_{k-1}) = i_0, where next(x) is the unique index y with 0 <= y < n and y is congruent to x + nums[x] modulo n; and either nums[i_j] > 0 for every j with 0 <= j < k, or nums[i_j] < 0 for every j with 0 <= j < k. If no such k and indices exist, then r = false.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0.

statement: The function returns a result r; equivalently, the call does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds, or arithmetic failure) for any input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0.

statement: The function returns a result r with r = false.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n = 1. Also -1000 <= nums[0] <= 1000 and nums[0] != 0.

statement: The function returns a result r. r = true if and only if nums[0] and nums[1] have the same sign (both positive or both negative) and both nums[0] and nums[1] are odd (equivalently, each is congruent to 1 modulo 2). In all other cases r = false.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). n = 2. For i = 0 and i = 1, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0.

statement: The function returns a result r with r = true.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 2 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0. Either nums[i] > 0 for every i with 0 <= i < n, or nums[i] < 0 for every i with 0 <= i < n. For every i with 0 <= i < n, n does not divide nums[i].

statement: Let r be the result on nums and r_rot be the result on rot. Both calls return results, and r_rot = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0. Let t be an integer with 0 <= t < n, and define rot by rot[i] = nums[(i + t) mod n] for 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let r be the result on nums and r_mirror be the result on mirror. Both calls return results, and r_mirror = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0. Define mirror by mirror[i] = -nums[n - 1 - i] for 0 <= i < n.

statement: Let r be the result on nums and r' be the result on nums'. Both calls return results, and r' = r.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0. Let nums' be another array of length n satisfying the same bounds and nonzero conditions, and such that for every i with 0 <= i < n, nums'[i] is congruent to nums[i] modulo n and nums'[i] has the same sign as nums[i] (both positive or both negative).

statement: Whenever the function returns true, for any valid witness cycle (i_0, ..., i_{k-1}) as in the main specification, every index i_j in it satisfies: n does not divide nums[i_j].
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. For every i with 0 <= i < n, -1000 <= nums[i] <= 1000 and nums[i] != 0.

statement: The function returns a result r. r = true if and only if n does not divide c. Equivalently, r = false exactly when c is congruent to 0 modulo n.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). 1 <= n <= 5000. There is a nonzero integer c with -1000 <= c <= 1000 such that nums[i] = c for every i with 0 <= i < n.
